blockers.description: CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT rather than left open. The planner reproduced the set -e hazard empirically: under 'set -e', 'cmd; test $? -eq 1' aborts at the git grep and never reaches test (its probe never printed REACHED-test; outer exit 1), while the 'if' form printed REACHED-end and exited 0. So this was a real defect, not a theoretical one, and all five absence gates were converted. The plan's own Shell conventions section now warns AGAINST the idiom rather than prescribing it -- it had gone stale in the same edit that introduced the fix.

decisions.decision: lc3 corrects SEVEN ci.yml sites plus one live spec docstring, not the one line the defect report named
decisions.rationale: Root-cause discipline plus the repo's own DOCS-09 precedent ('all SEVEN sites ... corrected in the SAME commit'). Five sites carry the presence-mechanism defect (:210, :1004, :1022, :1033, :1040); two carry the failure-implication defect (:1005-1006, :1030-1031); docs-same-os-claims.spec.ts:522 carries BOTH.

decisions.decision: The comment lock goes on the EXISTING row D of docs-same-os-claims.spec.ts, as two phrases -- no new row
decisions.rationale: That spec is table-driven (DOCS_08_SITES, iterated at :615-642) and its read is RAW, so it can see comments -- unlike dogfood-cross-os.spec.ts, whose codeLines filter strips every # line and makes a lock there vacuous by construction (its own policy note at :223-225 says so). Row D already owns this step. Pin 'UNCONDITIONAL cache.restoreCache' and '404 means the sidecar DID answer' -- the cause and the code discrimination, never the disjunction's incidental wording.

decisions.decision: The prose must distinguish MEASURED from REASONED, and this is the plan's top quality constraint
decisions.rationale: The presence disjunction ('restored OR saved') is MEASURED -- runs 30907575624 and 30910935382, both legs HIT, control returned 200. The failure-implication correction is REASONED from code and has NEVER been observed: the control's FAIL direction has no run behind it. A freshly-asserted wrong claim is worse than the inherited defect, which at least predates the evidence.

decisions.decision: The dead-sidecar negative gates are SENTENCE-scoped, never file-wide
decisions.rationale: Two of the four ci.yml occurrences are legitimate and must survive: :1015 (the historical record of the claim being corrected) and :1047 (the || true paragraph, where a dead sidecar genuinely DOES yield 000 -- the fact that makes the correction true). A file-wide == 0 gate would delete the evidence the correction rests on.
It is REQUIREMENTS.md's own word and the corrected prose may legitimately reuse it. Gating it would fire on correct work. The gate is narrowed to 'own save|just saved'.

decisions.decision: No behaviour change: acceptance set (200 alone), no-retry-loop, and step placement all UNCHANGED
decisions.rationale: Only the REASONS are wrong. :1040 is the one site whose stated reason is false for Case B; its replacement leads with a premise-independent reason (own_hash comes from integration-hash.txt, written by the run.json reader, so the step's INPUT does not exist before the Nx run). Placement itself is unchanged.

decisions.decision: h3b ran on the MAIN TREE with no worktree isolation, and lc3 should too
decisions.rationale: Single sequential plan means no parallelism to gain, and a junctioned node_modules makes check:action report FALSE bundle drift (esbuild rewrites module paths with no source edit) -- only the main tree gives a true bundle verdict. AGENTS.md's own decision rule says sequential-on-main.
